operations.name: map
operations.summary: Map a flat unstructured mesh onto a bent structured mesh
operations.description: Map a flat unstructured mesh onto a bent HEX8 structured mesh using isoparametric mapping. Automatically detects and aligns detail/bent axes by ranked bounding box lengths. Supports output and input mirroring, bbox-stretch elimination, optional prestress chaining, and selective part targeting. Preserves material and part definitions from flat source mesh.

params.name: single
params.description: Use single-threaded mode for mapping. Default is parallel processing.

params.name: force_positive
params.description: Force every mapped HEX8 Jacobian positive by swapping connectivity. Use when source mesh has unreliable handedness.

params.name: flip_x
params.description: Mirror output along global X axis. Swaps HEX8 connectivity when odd-parity flips would invert Jacobian.

params.name: flip_y
params.description: Mirror output along global Y axis. Can be combined with --flip-x and/or --flip-z.

params.name: flip_z
params.description: Mirror output along global Z axis. Can be combined with --flip-x and/or --flip-y.

params.name: flip_input_x
params.description: Pre-map detail flat mirror along X. Mirrors detail BEFORE mapping so features land on opposite face of bent target. Use for slit/hole face swap.

params.name: flip_input_y
params.description: Pre-map detail flat mirror along Y axis. Can be combined with --flip-input-x and/or --flip-input-z.

params.name: flip_input_z
params.description: Pre-map detail flat mirror along Z axis. Can be combined with --flip-input-x and/or --flip-input-y.

params.name: bbox_align
params.description: Auto-rescale to remove uniform stretch. 'source' rescales detail to bent ijk lengths; 'target' rescales bent to detail XYZ lengths; 'none' disables (default).

params.name: bbox_align_max_drift
params.description: Reject scaling if any axis ratio drifts beyond this percent. Default 2.0%.

params.name: target_pid
params.description: Target specific part IDs for mapping (comma or space separated). Default: all parts. Example: --target-pid '1,2,3' or --target-pids '1 2 3'.

params.name: bent_mesh
params.description: Bent structured reference mesh (LS-DYNA .k file). Must contain HEX8 elements.

params.name: flat_mesh
params.description: Flat unstructured mesh to be mapped (LS-DYNA .k file). CAD-derived with material/section definitions.

params.name: output
params.description: Output file path for mapped mesh (LS-DYNA .k). Contains remapped geometry with all source material/part definitions.

example.note: Basic mapping: flat mesh onto bent reference. Auto-detects axis alignment by ranked bounding box lengths.

alternative_invocations.description: YAML config file (single argument ending in .yaml or .yml)

prestress.output: Path to output dynain or CSV file
prestress.csv: Boolean, output CSV instead of dynain, default false

operations.notes:
CRITICAL GOTCHAS & DESIGN POINTS:

1. FLIP SEMANTICS — Two orthogonal mirroring subsystems:
   - flip_input_x/y/z: Mirror DETAIL FLAT BEFORE mapping. Features (slits, holes, asymmetric thickness) swap faces of bent target. Result coordinates unchanged. Useful for inner/outer surface swap independent of bent location.
   - flip_x/y/z: Mirror RESULT AFTER mapping. Negates output node coordinates. Applies post-mapping transformation.
   - Both can be combined. HEX8 connectivity swapped automatically on odd-parity flips to preserve Jacobian sign.

2. BBOX_ALIGN MODE & AXIS PAIRING:
   - Uses rank-based axis matching (smallest detail axis ↔ smallest bent axis) to survive axis permutations without explicit axis mapping.
   - 'source' mode: Scales detail flat to match bent ijk neutral lengths, then maps. Flat geometry slightly stretched per-axis. Temp file written (.__preproc_flat.k) for prestress reference.
   - 'target' mode: Scales bent to match detail XYZ lengths, then maps. Detail untouched. No temp file needed.
   - bbox_align_max_drift rejects scaling if any single axis ratio drifts beyond threshold (e.g., 2.0% = max ratio 1.02).

3. PRESTRESS CHAINING (YAML ONLY):
   - Available ONLY in YAML config form, not CLI positional form.
   - Runs AFTER mapping completes. Treats original flat mesh as reference, just-written mapped output as deformed.
   - If E/nu given in prestress block, overrides K-file materials entirely.
   - If prestress.enabled is true but output missing, returns error.
   - Reference mesh selection: if bbox_align=source, uses .__preproc_flat.k temp (already scaled/flipped); else uses original flat.

4. MESH REQUIREMENTS & TOPOLOGY:
   - bent mesh: MUST be structurally regular HEX8 grid (no mixed element types at mapping stage). Validated before mapping starts.
   - flat mesh: Can be unstructured HEX8, TET4, or other solid elements. Material/section/part cards from flat preserved in output.
   - Flat nodes outside bent domain issue warning (no error) and pass through unchanged.

5. AXIS AUTO-MAPPING:
   - Automatically detects which detail axis (X, Y, Z) pairs with which bent axis (I, J, K) by comparing bounding box lengths.
   - Reported in console output as "Auto Axis Mapping" diagnostic.
   - Survives detail/bent axis permutations (e.g., detail ZYX ↔ bent IJK).

6. JACOBIAN & ELEMENT QUALITY:
   - Mapping preserves source mesh (flat) winding/orientation. If mixed positive/negative Jacobians detected, use force_positive=true to unify.
   - Output statistics show min/max/avg Jacobian, count of invalid (negative) elements, and reoriented elements (connectivity swaps for sign match).

7. PARALLEL PROCESSING (DEFAULT):
   - parallel=true (default) uses OpenMP for node mapping. Set to false for reproducibility, debugging, or environments without OpenMP.

8. PRESTRESS REFERENCE WITH PREPROCESSING:
   - If bbox_align=source is used, maps generates .__preproc_flat.k temp file. Prestress reference MUST use this scaled flat (automatically selected by map).
   - If prestress runs against original unscaled flat, it will reintroduce the stretch that bbox-align just removed.

9. CLI vs YAML PRECEDENCE:
   - CLI flags always override YAML values (CLI takes precedence).
   - Example: 'KooRemapper map config.yaml --flip-x' overrides any flip_x setting in YAML.

10. TARGET_PID FILTERING:
    - Available ONLY via CLI flags (--target-pid / --target-pids), NOT in YAML.
    - Accepts comma or space-separated list. Example: --target-pids '1,2,3' or --target-pids '1 2 3'.
    - Only nodes referenced by elements in target PIDs are mapped; all others (other PIDs, orphan nodes) pass through unchanged.
    - Empty target set (default) maps all parts.

11. ENVIRONMENT & DEBUG:
    - Set KOO_MAP_DEBUG=1 for detailed internal orientation/axis-pairing diagnostics to stderr.

12. GRID LOOKUP OPTIMIZATION:
    - Interior grid acceleration structure optionally built during mapping. Reported in "Interior grid lookup" line showing fill percentage and active status."

operations.name: shellmap
operations.summary: Map a flat detail mesh onto a bent QUAD4 shell reference mesh
operations.description: Maps a flat detail mesh (solid or shell elements) onto a bent QUAD4 shell reference mesh by unfolding the shell to preserve edge lengths, then mapping the flat detail onto the bent surface. Automatically detects or accepts explicit thickness for Z-offset positioning. Best suited for developable surfaces with single curvature (cylinders, cones).

params.name: bent_shell
params.description: Bent shell reference mesh with QUAD4 elements (k-file)

params.name: flat_detail
params.description: Flat detail mesh to be mapped (solid or shell elements, k-file)

params.name: output
params.description: Output file path for the mapped mesh

params.name: thickness
params.description: Shell thickness for Z-offset mapping (default: auto-detect from flat mesh Z-range)

example.note: Maps a flat 8x4 detail mesh onto a 30-degree cylindrical arc shell. Auto-detects thickness from flat mesh Z-range (-0.1 to +0.1 = 0.2). Output contains mapped quad4 or hex elements on the bent surface.

operations.notes:
- **QUAD4-only**: bent_shell MUST contain exclusively QUAD4 elements; TRIA3 or other types are not supported. Validation happens in bentShell.validate(validationError).
- **Thickness auto-detection**: When thickness ≤0, code computes Z-range of flat_detail's bounding box. If Z-range < 1e-15, interprets mesh as shell geometry (thickness→0). Log message: "Auto-detected thickness from Z-range: X".
- **Developable surface warning**: After unfolding, if max distortion > 5%, code warns: "High area distortion detected (>5%). Surface may not be developable." Non-developable surfaces (double curvature) produce mapping artifacts.
- **Axis swap**: If flat_detail bounding box aspect ratio doesn't match unfolded shell, mapper auto-swaps X↔Y axes. Logged: "Auto-alignment: axes swapped (flat X<->Y) to match unfolded shell".
- **Unmapped nodes**: If nodes fall outside shell domain during 3D projection, they remain at their in-plane (u,v) position with thickness offset. Count logged as warning: "N nodes could not be mapped (outside shell domain)".
- **Non-geometry card preservation**: Output k-file includes all MAT_*, PART, SECTION, and other non-geometry cards from flat_detail source (via writeFileWithSource withSourceCards=true).
- **CLI-only operation**: No YAML/assemble pipeline support; shellmap is standalone positional CLI command only. The assemble 'replace' operation uses different internal logic (shell unfolding + mapping), not shellmap directly.
- **Parser parsing**: Iterates argv[2..argc) collecting non-flag strings as positional args; only --thickness is recognized as flag. Unknown flags or options are silently skipped (not validated). Requires exactly 3 positional args.

operations.name: unfold
operations.summary: Generate a flat unfolded mesh from a bent structured HEX8 mesh by computing arc-length along the centerline.
operations.description: Generate a flat (unfolded) mesh from a bent structured HEX8 mesh by computing arc-length along the centerline. The algorithm automatically detects structured grid dimensions (I, J, K), computes arc-length along the arc axis, and preserves cross-section sizes in the perpendicular directions. The output maintains identical topology to the input but with coordinates adjusted to a flat configuration suitable for reference geometry in mapping operations.

params.name: bent_mesh
params.description: The bent structured mesh (LS-DYNA .k file with HEX8 elements)

params.name: output_flat
params.description: Output file path for the flat (unfolded) mesh

example.note: Reads a bent HEX8-element mesh (arc30_bent.k with 3x21x20 grid) and generates a flat reference mesh with arc-length unwrapped along X, output topology identical to input

operations.notes: CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS: (1) Input must be a STRUCTURED HEX8 mesh (not unstructured). The operation auto-detects grid dimensions and fails if connectivity is not regular. (2) No optional flags or YAML configuration — unfold is purely positional CLI. Takes exactly 2 arguments. (3) Output topology identical to input — same element connectivity, same part IDs and materials preserved. (4) Axis permutation automatic: the operation identifies the arc axis (longest cumulative edge length), width axis (J), and thickness axis (K). For closed-loop bent meshes, the operation auto-detects and shifts the apex (lowest-curvature point) to the middle of the unfold for symmetric output. (5) Designed as reference generator for the 'map' command — use output with: KooRemapper map bent_mesh.k detailed_flat.k output_bent.k (6) Console output reports grid size (I×J×K) and flat extents (length-I in arc units, length-J, length-K in original units). (7) Validation runs automatically: validates HEX8 structure; reports errors if mesh is non-structured or malformed.

keys.desc: Input bent structured mesh in LS-DYNA .k format. Must be a regular HEX8-element structured mesh (3D grid with identical topology in I, J, K directions). The mesh does not require uniform edge lengths but must have analyzable centerline geometry.

Output path for the generated flat (unfolded) mesh in LS-DYNA .k format. The mesh will have the same node and element count as input, with identical topology but coordinates transformed to flat configuration (arc-length along I, cross-section preserved in J-K plane).

operations.name: generate
operations.summary: Generate example test meshes (curved/bent types or box solids) with customizable grid dimensions.
operations.description: Generate example test meshes or uniform hexahedral (HEX8) solid boxes. Supports two invocation modes: (1) type-based mode generates curved geometry bent-flat mesh pairs (teardrop, arc, torus, wave, etc.) as standalone command; (2) box mode generates uniform solid boxes from YAML config within assemble operations, serving as the initial base_model when no base_model is specified.

params.description: Number of elements in J (second parametric) direction. Only used with type mode.

example.note: Generates torus_bent.k, torus_flat.k, torus_flat_fine.k, torus_flat_tet.k with 10x5x5 elements. For box generation use: KooRemapper generate box /path/to/box_gen.yaml

operations.notes:
OPERATIONAL MODES:
---
1. STANDALONE TYPE MODE (command-line or 'generate box' invocation):
   - Used OUTSIDE assemble operations to generate test meshes quickly
   - Command: `KooRemapper generate <type> [--dim-i N] [--dim-j M] [--dim-k K] <output_prefix>`
   - Generates FOUR output files: {prefix}_bent.k, {prefix}_flat.k, {prefix}_flat_fine.k, {prefix}_flat_tet.k
   - Flags: --dim-i (default 10), --dim-j (default 5), --dim-k (default 5) control element grid in parametric directions
   - Box sub-command: `KooRemapper generate box <config.yaml>` generates one .k file from YAML

2. ASSEMBLE BOX MODE (operations[].type = generate):
   - Used AS FIRST OPERATION when base_model is NOT specified
   - Must be the FIRST operation in the operations list to serve as initial base model
   - Generates a single uniform HEX8 box solid (shape=box only)
   - Keys read: shape, lx, ly, lz, nx, ny, nz, rho, E, nu, mid, secid, pid, part_title
   - Creates *MAT_ELASTIC, *SECTION_SOLID, *PART, *NODE, *ELEMENT_SOLID cards automatically
   - Subsequent operations (restack, offset, etc.) can then operate on pid=1 (or specified pid)

YAML PARSING (assemble mode):
---
- All keys are case-sensitive and use underscores (not hyphens)
- Numeric values are parsed via std::stod (double) or std::stoi (integer); unparseable values default to defaults above
- String values (shape, part_title) are trimmed and quoted-stripped
- No validation error thrown on invalid input; default values silently used instead

CONSTRAINTS & DEFAULTS:
---
- shape: only "box" supported in assemble; empty string defaults to "box"
- nx, ny, nz: must be >= 1; generates (nx+1)×(ny+1)×(nz+1) nodes, nx×ny×nz elements
- mid, secid, pid: must be positive (0 auto-corrected to 1 on write); no duplicate check
- Element formulation: HEX8 (8-node solid), section elform=1 (fully integrated)
- Material model: *MAT_ELASTIC (linear elastic isotropic)
- Node numbering: 1-based, sequential in Z-major order (iz varies slowest, ix fastest)
- Element numbering: 1-based, same Z-major order; HEX8 node order = bottom CCW then top CCW (standard ABAQUS/LS-DYNA convention)

MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE / DEPENDENCIES:
---
- shape must be "box" (waterdrop, teardrop, etc. only in standalone type mode, not assemble)
- Cannot specify both shape= and type= (different command invocations)
- Part, section, material IDs (pid, secid, mid) should be unique in the model; no auto-increment collision avoidance

WATERDROP SPECIAL CASE (standalone type mode only):
---
- type: waterdrop
- Automatically uses lx=160.0, ly=70.0, lz=1.0 (foldable display geometry, 160mm fold direction, 70mm width, 1mm thick)
- Sets waterdropFoldRadius=2.0 (U-bend radius in mm), waterdropFlatRatio=0.45 (45% flat on each end, 10% fold in middle)
- Generates bent/flat pair suitable for flexible/foldable smartphone display drop-test modeling

OUTPUT FILES (standalone type mode):
---
- {prefix}_bent.k: curved bent geometry (parametric ijk surface mapped to 3D XYZ)
- {prefix}_flat.k: undeformed flat reference mesh
- {prefix}_flat_fine.k: refined unstructured quad mesh (2x subdivision) for mapping sensitivity studies
- {prefix}_flat_tet.k: tetrahedral (TET4) variant for non-structured test cases

OUTPUT FILE (box mode):
---
- Single .k file specified in YAML 'output' key (or --output flag)
- Must have .k extension; auto-added if missing
- Contains *MAT_ELASTIC, *SECTION_SOLID, *PART, *NODE (*ELEMENT_SOLID, *END

operations.summary: YAML 설정으로부터 평탄 또는 곡선 가변 밀도 메시 생성
operations.description: Generate variable density mesh from YAML configuration. Supports flat meshing with 5-zone element distribution along I-axis, or curved meshing following Catmull-Rom/B-spline centerline. Automatic scaling to reference dimensions if provided.

params.name: config
params.description: YAML 설정 파일 (type, reference, variable_density 또는 centerline_points 포함)

operations.notes: FLAT TYPE BEHAVIOR: The 5 zones (zone1_dense_start, zone2_increasing, zone3_sparse, zone4_decreasing, zone5_dense_end) partition the I direction. Total I length = sum of zone lengths (before scaling). Total I elements = sum of zone num_elements. If reference mesh or dimensions provided, all zone lengths are scaled proportionally to match reference I dimension, unless --no-scale flag suppresses scaling. J and K elements are always uniform. CURVED TYPE BEHAVIOR: Requires centerline_points with minimum 2 points. Interpolation creates smooth curve through (or near) points depending on interpolation type. If reference mesh provided, arc length and cross-section (width, thickness) are auto-scaled to reference I, J, K dimensions; otherwise uses cross_section.width/thickness directly (defaults 1.0 each if omitted). elements_along_curve, elements_j (alias for width), elements_k (alias for thickness) control element counts. GROWTH_TYPE: Linear = uniform element spacing within zone; Geometric = element size varies multiplicatively; Exponential = exponential progression. Used for transition zones (2, 4) to smoothly vary element density. SCALING: Command-line --ref option overrides config's reference.flat_mesh. If both --ref and reference in YAML present, --ref takes precedence. --no-scale disables all scaling; zone lengths used as absolute dimensions. COMMON GOTCHAS: (1) Centerline_points must be YAML list format (each point on separate line with '- [x, y]'); inline [x,y] on one line not parsed. (2) Cross_section (width, thickness) ignored if reference mesh/dimensions provided. (3) Growth_type applies only to zones; sparse/dense zone distinction is determined by num_elements relative to neighbors, not by growth_type. (4) All numeric values (length, num_elements, width, thickness) must be positive. Zero or negative values cause validation failure. (5) If type not specified, defaults to 'flat'. Curved requires explicit type: curved in YAML.

operations.notes: **Invocation**: Positional CLI with 3 required arguments + 1 optional flag. Syntax: `KooRemapper strain [--type TYPE] <ref_mesh.k> <def_mesh.k> <output.csv>`. **Topology requirement**: ref_mesh and def_mesh must have identical node IDs, element connectivity, and part structure; only nodal coordinates are allowed to differ. **Output CSV columns**: element_id, node_ids..., Exx, Eyy, Ezz, Exy, Exz, Eyz, E1, E2, E3, von_mises_eq, volumetric_strain. **Console statistics**: After calculation, reports max/avg von Mises strain, max/min volumetric strain, max/min principal strains. **No material input needed**: Unlike prestress, strain computation does not require Young's modulus or Poisson ratio—it is purely geometric deformation analysis. **Large deformation guidance**: 'engineering' is valid for ~<10% strain (small deformation assumption); 'green' or 'log' recommended for >10% strain. 'log' is frame-indifferent and symmetric in tension/compression for large ductile flows. **Practical use**: Typical inputs are bent_shell.k (reference) vs. measured warpage/formed shape (deformed), or pre-assembly geometry (reference) vs. post-assembly geometry (deformed with prestress/squeeze/bend applied).

operations.notes: Material priority: command-line --E/--nu (highest) completely override K-file materials; if neither provided, reads *PART→*MAT_ELASTIC mappings from ref_mesh. If no material found, stress output is zero but strain is always computed. Both meshes must have identical topology (node IDs, element IDs, connectivity); if one mesh is the result of mapping (e.g., KooRemapper map output), verify node/element IDs match ref_mesh. Output always includes a .k file (deformed mesh with *INCLUDE directive) plus .dynain; remove the extension from 'output' argument—the tool auto-appends .dynain and .k. Flip correction: if meshes have odd-parity mirror flips (e.g., HEX8 node order swapped), apply the same flip to ref_mesh before passing to prestress to ensure consistent strain computation (reflection-invariant E' = R E R^T). Green-Lagrange strain is for large deformations (bending, forming); engineering strain for small deformations.

operations.summary: Extract free surface faces from solid HEX8/TET4 mesh as ELEMENT_SHELL (QUAD4)
operations.description: Extracts the free (outer) surface of a solid HEX8/TET4 mesh as shell QUAD4 elements. A free face is one shared by exactly one element (interior faces shared by 2+ elements are dropped). Supports directional filtering (top/bottom/all) using Z-centroid heuristics and optional mid-surface mode that pairs top/bottom nodes by XY proximity to create a single averaged shell layer.

params.name: solid_file
params.description: Input solid mesh file (HEX8/TET4 elements, LS-DYNA K-file)

params.name: output_shell

params.description: Filter extraction by part ID (0 = all parts)

params.description: Part ID for emitted shell elements

params.name: mid_surface
params.description: Enable mid-surface mode: pair top/bottom nodes by XY proximity, create averaged shell layer (requires both top and bottom faces)

example.note: Extracts all free surfaces from solid mesh and emits as PID 1 shell elements. For mid-surface mode on a layered part, add --mid-surface flag to pair top/bottom faces.

operations.notes:
**Free face detection**: A face is considered free if it belongs to exactly 1 element. Interior faces (shared by 2+ elements) are discarded. Face winding order is preserved from the first element containing that face (used for later orientation).

**Top/bottom discrimination**: Uses unweighted centroid Z of face versus parent element centroid Z. If dz = face_z - elem_z: dz > 0 → top; dz < 0 → bottom; dz ≈ 0 (degenerate, face exactly on element plane) → neither top nor bottom, only included in 'all' mode.

**Mid-surface mode algorithm**: (1) Collect all unique node IDs on top and bottom free face sets. (2) Build 2D spatial hash from bottom-side nodes with cell size = bbox_diagonal / sqrt(node_count) (0.5–1.5× typical element size). (3) For each top node, find closest bottom node in 3×3 hash window (XY distance only). If no match found, node is skipped with warning. (4) Create mid-node at average of matched top/bottom pair coordinates (XYZ all three dimensions averaged). (5) Remap top face winding to mid node IDs. If a top node has no match, entire face is skipped.

**Degenerate triangles (TRIA3)**: Written as degenerate QUAD4 with N4=N3 per LS-DYNA convention (4th node = 3rd node). Input TET4 meshes with TRIA3 boundary faces are auto-detected via isTriangle(n[3]==n[2] || n[3]==0 || n[3]==n[0]) logic.

**Mutually exclusive options**: None. However, 'face' parameter is logically ignored when mid_surface=true (mid-surface mode uses top+bottom regardless).

**Common gotchas**:
- mid_surface requires BOTH top and bottom face sets present; if either is empty, command fails with error "requires both top and bottom free faces (found top=N, bottom=M)".
- Top/bottom detection is Z-only, ignoring X/Y symmetry; if mesh spans multiple Z-levels with layered structure not aligned to Z, discrimination may fail.
- Spatial hash cell size in mid-surface mode is adaptive; with very coarse or very dense meshes, pairing may fail or pair distant nodes. No user control over cell size.
- Output K-file contains ONLY *NODE and *ELEMENT_SHELL blocks; input solid HEX8/TET4 elements and interior nodes are NOT preserved (external post-processing required if retention needed).
- Node IDs in output are those used by emitted shells only; unused nodes from input are dropped.
- If all top/bottom nodes match, output node count = original node count (mid_surface creates new IDs but reuses spatial locations). If partial match, output node count < 2× input top/bottom nodes.

operations.notes: **핵심 제약사항:** (1) swelling과 eps_x/y/z는 동일 파트에서 동시 사용 불가. (2) eps 모드(응력 계산)는 재료 필수: YAML material 또는 K-파일 *MAT_ELASTIC. (3) swelling 모드는 K-파일 *MAT_* 카드 필수 (MID를 *PART에서 자동 읽음). (4) strain_mode=true일 때 응력 계산 안 함 (재료 불필요). **동작 모드:** 응력 모드(기본): eps_x/y/z로 노드 변형, Hooke의 법칙으로 응력 계산 → *INITIAL_STRESS_SOLID 생성. 변형률 모드(strain_mode=true): eps_x/y/z로 노드 변형, 역방향 변형률만 기록 → *INITIAL_STRAIN_SOLID 생성 (재료 무관). 열팽창 모드(swelling): 노드 이동 없음, 대신 *MAT_ADD_THERMAL_EXPANSION + *INITIAL_TEMPERATURE_NODE 삽입, LS-DYNA가 런타임에 열변형 적용. **재료 우선순위:** YAML material 섹션 > K-파일 *MAT_ELASTIC. **출력 파일:** <prefix>.k = 압축 메시 + 열팽창 카드 + DR 카드. <prefix>_dynain.dat = *INITIAL_STRESS_SOLID (eps 파트만, swelling 파트 제외). **공식:** 바운딩박스 중심 c에 대해 x' = c + (1+eps_i) * (x - c). 응력 σxx = -(λ+2μ)eps_x - λ(eps_y+eps_z) (라메 상수 기반).

operations.name: bend
operations.summary: Apply bending deformation and optional prestress to a part.
operations.description: The bend operation applies bending deformation and optional initial stress to part(s) using deflection functions (formula-based, single dat file, or dat file pair). Supports three deflection sources: formula expressions, single .dat grid, and paired dat files (top/bottom surfaces). Two modes: deform (node repositioning with backward prestress to maintain bent state after dynamic relaxation) and stress (forward-only prestress without node movement).

params.name: config
params.description: YAML 설정 객체. base_model, output, operations[] 배열 포함. 각 operation은 type:bend로 지정.

example.note: 실행: KooRemapper bend formula_deform.yaml → formula_deform_output.k 생성. source=formula 모드에서는 expression 필수; source=dat 모드에서는 dat_file 필수; source=dat_pair 모드에서는 dat_top, dat_bottom 필수.

operations.notes: Mutually exclusive source paths: set exactly ONE of (expression | dat_file | dat_pair). target_pid=0 means all parts in model; target_pid > 0 targets single part; target_pids=[] list targets multiple parts (overrides target_pid if non-empty). plane=xy maps x1→X, x2→Y, normal→Z; yz maps x1→Y, x2→Z, normal→X; zx maps x1→Z, x2→X, normal→Y. Formula variables x1, x2 are normalized [0,1] relative to bbox min; L1, L2 are bbox extents in those axes; pi=3.14159... Supported functions: sin, cos, tan, sqrt, exp, log, abs, pow(base,exp). mode=deform applies node displacement, then computes backward prestress (dynain_embed=true embeds *INITIAL_STRESS_SOLID in output .k). mode=stress computes forward prestress (initial curvature state); nodes stay unchanged; DR can then deform toward bent state. Material (E, nu) required for any stress output; must be specified at config root level. dat_file format: ASCII grid, rows from top→bottom, columns left→right, space/tab separated. dat_pair mode computes thickness-dependent curvature from top–bottom difference. If dynamic_relaxation=true and mode=deform, the deformation locks in place (backward prestress cancels). If mode=stress, DR flattens the shape (forward prestress unfolds it back to bent state). targetPid and targetPids are validated: either targetPid > 0 OR targetPid = 0 (all) OR non-empty targetPids array; cannot be -1 alone (reserved for internal use). All path parameters (dat_file, dat_top, dat_bottom) resolve relative to config directory unless absolute (/ or Windows drive letter)."

keys.desc: Part ID to deform. 0 = all parts, positive integer = specific part ID. Mutually exclusive with target_pids array; if target_pids is non-empty, target_pid is ignored.
List of part IDs to deform (e.g., [1, 2, 3]). When non-empty, overrides target_pid.

Bending plane in 3D mesh. xy = deform in Z (normal to XY plane); yz = deform in X (normal to YZ plane); zx = deform in Y (normal to ZX plane). Defines the in-plane axes (x1, x2) and normal-axis mapping for formula evaluation and curvature computation.

deform = move nodes via deflection field + backward prestress (shape locked after dynamic relaxation); stress = forward prestress only (no node movement; dynamic relaxation flattens structure which bends back).
Deflection input source. formula = mathematical expression w(x1, x2); dat = single gridded deflection file; dat_pair = two files (top surface, bottom surface; difference computes curvature).

Mathematical expression for w(x1, x2) deflection field. Required when source=formula. Variables: x1, x2 (normalized in-plane coords, 0–1 within bbox), L1, L2 (in-plane bbox dimensions), pi. Functions: sin, cos, tan, sqrt, exp, log, abs, pow. Example: '1.0*sin(pi*x1/L1)*sin(pi*x2/L2)'.

Path to deflection grid file (.dat). Required when source=dat. Format: whitespace-separated columns (x1 direction: min→max), rows from x2_max→min (top→bottom). Deflection values interpolated bilinearly to mesh nodes via bbox mapping.
Path to top-surface deflection file (.dat). Required when source=dat_pair. Used with dat_bottom to compute curvature (midplane = average, curvature = difference field / thickness).
Path to bottom-surface deflection file (.dat). Required when source=dat_pair. Used with dat_top to compute curvature. Both files must have identical grid dimensions.

operations.name: indent
operations.summary: Apply indentation or embossing deformation and compute prestress with polygon or spline punch shapes.
operations.description: Apply indentation or embossing deformation and compute optional prestress with polygon or spline punch shapes. Depth > 0 for indentation (inward deformation), depth < 0 for embossing (outward deformation). Supports both solid and shell elements with optional bending stress calculation output to *INITIAL_STRESS_SOLID (LS-DYNA).

params.name: config
params.description: Complete YAML configuration object containing base_model, output, optional material/dynain settings, and operations array with indent specifications

example.note: 실행 검증된 예제 (입력: block.k, shell_plate.k)

operations.notes: Coordinate system: shape points are 2D coordinates in the indentation plane. For plane='xy', use [x,y]. For plane='yz', use [y,z]. For plane='zx', use [z,x]. Direction must be perpendicular to plane (e.g., plane='xy' with direction='+z' or '-z'). Profile uses quarter-arc fillets with curvatures computed from r1, r2, depth. Stress calculation applies BEFORE node deformation (like bend); strain capping uses strainLimit/(thickness/2) upper bound for curvature at singularities. operations.name: formstrain
operations.summary: Compute plastic strain from shell mesh dihedral angles using curvature estimation.
operations.description: Computes equivalent plastic strain (EPS) from shell mesh dihedral angles using curvature estimation. Maps local bending curvature (kappa = theta/L) at each QUAD4 element to plastic equivalent strain via EPS = (t/2*kappa - sigy/E)_max, then embeds result as *INITIAL_STRAIN_SHELL in output LS-DYNA .k file. Requires shell elements with material yield stress for strain calculation.

params.name: config
params.description: Full YAML configuration object with base_model, output, and operations array

example.note: Example shows a single operation targeting PID 1 with explicit thickness override and curvature floor. Omit target_pid to auto-detect all shell parts; omit shell_thickness/min_curvature for defaults.

operations.notes:
MATERIAL & SECTION REQUIREMENTS:
- Requires shell parts with *ELEMENT_SHELL QUAD4 elements only (TRIA3 not supported).
- Must have associated *SECTION_SHELL card with T1 (thickness) > 0 per part.
- Must have associated *MAT_PIECEWISE_LINEAR_PLASTICITY (MAT_024) with SIGY (yield stress) > 0; other material types (MAT_ELASTIC, MAT_JOHNSON_COOK, etc.) are skipped with a logged message.
- E (Young's modulus) and SIGY are read from MAT_024 Card 1 Fields 3 & 5.

AUTO-DETECTION LOGIC (when target_pid = 0):
- Scans all parts in base_model.
- For each part: checks if SECTION_SHELL exists AND thickness > 0, AND material is MAT_024 with SIGY > 0.
- Parts not meeting all three conditions are silently skipped (logged as info, not error).

CURVATURE CALCULATION:
- For each QUAD4 element pair sharing an edge: computes dihedral angle θ from element normals (via diagonal cross product).
- Curvature κ = θ / L where L = centroid-to-centroid distance (in model units, typically mm).
- Per-element curvature = max(κ_edge_1, κ_edge_2, κ_edge_3, κ_edge_4). Free boundary edges (no neighbor) contribute 0.
- Plastic strain EPS = max(0, κ*t/2 - SIGY/E) where t is shell thickness.

OUTPUT KEYWORD:
- *INITIAL_STRAIN_SHELL written with NPLANE=1, NTHICK=2 (dual integration points for top/bottom surfaces).
- Both top (T=+1) and bottom (T=-1) surfaces receive identical EPS (symmetric bending assumption).
- STRESS fields (sigxx, sigyy, …) set to zero (springback-relaxed state; formstrain provides history via plastic strain only).

MULTI-OPERATION MERGING:
- When multiple operations (e.g., indent + formstrain) write to same elements, EPS values merged via max(), not sum.
- Stress values sum when present (indent adds stress; formstrain adds 0).

LOGGING & VALIDATION:
- When loading, info message lists each processed part: "FormStrain PID <pid>: t=<thickness> SIGY=<sigy> E=<E> → <element_count> elements with EPS".
- Normal consistency check: edges with normal dot product < -0.5 (likely flipped normals) are skipped; warning counter incremented. CAD meshes generally have correct normals; no auto-repair.
- Missing material or thickness produces info log (not error); that part is skipped.

MATHEMATICAL MODEL:
- EPS assumes pure bending (no extension/compression); inappropriate for complex forming (deep drawing, coining).
- Strain path independent: only final curvature used; intermediate forming history ignored.
- Perfectly plastic model: ε_plastic = max(0, strain - sigy/E). Real strain-hardening materials may require explicit curve (MAT_024 hardening table) which is not used here (conservative estimate).

EXAMPLE WORKFLOW:
1. Create/obtain bent shell mesh (e.g., press-formed bracket, shielding can).
2. Ensure parts have SECTION_SHELL and MAT_024 material with SIGY > 0.
3. Run with minimal YAML:
   base_model: bent_can.k
   output: result
   operations:
     - type: formstrain
4. Output result.k has *INITIAL_STRAIN_SHELL with EPS per element for use in subsequent impact/drop analysis.

GOTCHAS & LIMITATIONS:
- QUAD4 ONLY: TRIA3 shells silently skipped (no conversion).
- MAT_024 only: MAT_ELASTIC, MAT_ELASTIC_PLASTIC_HYDRO, etc. will not provide SIGY; parts using those materials are auto-skipped.
- Mesh-dependent: element-to-element curvature via dihedral angles; coarse mesh underestimates curvature; fine mesh better fidelity.
- No springback residual stress: EPS field models strain history; stress output is zero (assumes relaxed state post-forming).
- Noise sensitivity: flat regions (κ ≈ 0) produce very small EPS; min_curvature threshold helps; if too high, genuine gentle curves are zeroed.

operations.name: warpage
operations.summary: 측정된 변형 데이터를 셸 또는 솔리드 부품에 적용합니다
operations.description: Applies out-of-plane warpage deformation to mesh nodes based on measured 2D grid data (DAT/CSV). Supports two modes: prestress (generates initial stress via curvature analysis) and deform (direct node displacement). Bilinear interpolation maps the 2D measurement grid (minimum 3×3) to 3D mesh nodes across any orientation plane.

params.name: config
params.description: 전체 YAML 설정 객체. base_model, output, operations 포함

example.note: 실행 검증된 예제 (입력: wave_flat.k, warpage_3x3.dat)

operations.notes:
CRITICAL GOTCHAS:

1. **data_bbox vs part bbox**: If data_bbox is omitted, the operation auto-maps part geometry 1:1 to grid coordinates. This is correct only if part bbox dimensions align with grid extent. If data was measured in a different coordinate system, explicitly set data_bbox to avoid 1:1 assumption errors.

2. **Mask interpolation**: Values exactly equal to mask_value (within 1e-6) are flagged as invalid. Isolated masked regions that cannot be interpolated from neighbors will fail the load. >50% masking triggers a warning.

3. **Deflection axis sign**: Use explicit ±z/±x/±y. Unsigned z/x/y default to positive direction. The deflection is applied in physical coordinates AFTER the grid interpolation, so sign is part-global, not grid-local.

4. **Unit conversion chain**: dat_file values [um/mm/m] → unit_scale multiplier → * morph_factor → deflection applied to node position. For example, if dat_file contains 0.5 and unit=um, morph_factor=2.0, the node moves 0.5 * 1e-3 * 2.0 = 0.001 mm.

5. **Plane-axis coupling**: Plane (xy/yz/zx) defines which 2D axes of the grid map to mesh coordinates. Deflection must be perpendicular to the plane. E.g., plane=xy + deflection_axis=z is valid; plane=xy + deflection_axis=x is invalid (would deflect in-plane).

6. **Prestress mode requires material**: E > 0 and 0 < nu < 0.5 must be set at operation or assembly level. Curvatures are computed via finite differences; finite_strain=true adds nonlinear (∂w/∂x)² strain terms.

7. **Finite strain theory**: Only affects prestress mode. Von Kármán (true) captures membrane coupling for large deflections. Kirchhoff (false) is linear; appropriate for small deflections (w << thickness).

8. **Grid minimum size**: Minimum 3×3 grid required; maximum 1000×1000. File must be rectangular (all rows same column count).

9. **Bilinear interpolation assumes monotonic axis ordering** in the grid file. The grid is indexed as data[row][col] = data[i][j]; row indices map to v-axis, columns to u-axis in the normalized [0,1]×[0,1] space.

10. **Added elements**: Warpage collects both base mesh and addedElements_ nodes (from prior operations like replace/restack) belonging to target_pid.

MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE / INCOMPATIBLE OPTIONS:
- Cannot use both data_bbox and auto-map (only one is active per operation).
- mode=deform ignores material (E, nu); mode=prestress requires them.
- finite_strain only applies to prestress mode.

WORKFLOW NOTES:
- Warpage is typically applied AFTER replace/restack operations in the operations list so it can access the assembled geometry.
- For shell elements, thickness is auto-detected from *SECTION_SHELL or explicitly provided in debug output.
- Curvature calculation uses centered finite differences; edges use one-sided differences.

Supports fixed directions (±x/±y/±z), adaptive surface normals (±normal), variable thickness formulas, region filtering, multi-layer generation, and per-layer material definitions.

example.note: 실행 검증된 예제 (입력: arc30_flat.k)

operations.notes:
CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS AND GOTCHAS:

(1) REQUIRED PARAMETERS:
    - source_pid, offset_direction, thickness (unless thickness_formula), num_layers, connection_mode are mandatory
    - Missing any triggers validation error

(2) CONNECTION MODES:
    - tied: shares nodes at interface (lowest cost, zero gap)
    - czm: inserts cohesive elements with czm_material_card (requires *MAT_COHESIVE_*)
    - contact: duplicates nodes, user must add *CONTACT_* afterward
    - connection_mode="czm" REQUIRES czm_material_card; without it, validation fails

(3) ELEMENT TYPES AND RESTRICTIONS:
    - solid (HEX8): all features supported (tied/czm/contact, multi-layer, normal offset)
    - tshell (TSHELL): tied/contact only, NO czm mode
    - shell (QUAD4): tied/contact only, NO czm mode
    - When element_type is tshell/shell, shell_thickness MUST be set or defaults to thickness

(4) OFFSET DIRECTION:
    - +normal/-normal: auto-detects surface normal per element (best for curved surfaces; use with use_local_normals=true for better quality)
    - ±x/±y/±z: fixed global direction (simpler, faster)
    - v1.1.0+: -normal direction fixed (prior versions had negative Jacobian bugs)

(5) THICKNESS & LAYERS:
    - thickness: uniform per-layer thickness; with num_layers=3, creates 3 layers each of (thickness/3)
    - thickness_formula: if set, overrides thickness; supports x,y,z variables (e.g., "1.0 + 0.01*x")
    - num_layers must be ≥ 1
    - Multi-layer with different materials: use material_cards[] (array), one entry per layer

(6) MATERIAL CARD MAGIC:
    - Use @MID@ placeholder in material_card; auto-replaced with assigned material ID
    - Use @CZM_MID@ placeholder in czm_material_card; auto-replaced with CZM material ID
    - If new_mid=0, MID auto-increments; if new_mid > 0, uses that ID
    - Multi-layer material_cards[] must have length == num_layers
    - material_card and material_cards[] are mutually exclusive

(7) REGION FILTERS:
    - bbox_xmin/max, bbox_ymin/max, bbox_zmin/max: bounding box filter (all 6 values optional)
    - node_id_min/max: only offset nodes in this range (0 = disabled)
    - element_id_min/max: only offset elements in this range (0 = disabled)
    - Multiple filters can be combined (logical AND)
    - Filters apply to SOURCE elements; offset surfaces inherit the subset

(8) QUALITY WARNINGS:
    - Aspect Ratio > 10: warning; > 20: error
    - Jacobian < 0.1: warning; < 1e-10: error (negative = degenerate)
    - Warping > 30°: warning; > 45°: error
    - -normal offset on highly concave surfaces may cause self-intersection → check warnings

(9) PHASE/VERSION FEATURES:
    - use_local_normals, shell_offset, shell_thickness: Phase 2+
    - region filters (bbox_*, node_id_*, element_id_*): Phase 3+
    - thickness_formula: Phase 4+
    - prestress_mode="dual_offset": Phase 3+ (advanced)
    - material_cards[]: Phase 3+

(10) SOURCE ELEMENT SUPPORT:
    - Solid source elements: HEX8, TET4 (TET4 output quality degrades; HEX8 recommended)
    - Shell source elements: QUAD4, TRIA3 (auto-detected and handled)
    - Cannot use shell elements generated by prior offset in same operations[] list (PID tracking limitation)

(11) YAML STRUCTURE:
    - operations[] array; each offset entry is one offset operation
    - Can chain multiple offset operations (e.g., offset PID 1 → PID 10, then offset PID 10 → PID 11)
    - Base model, output, and operations are at root level

(12) @MID@ SUBSTITUTION:
    - material_card: "*MAT_ELASTIC ... @MID@ ... " → auto-replaces @MID@ with new_mid (or auto ID)
    - Each occurrence of @MID@ replaced; OK to have multiple @MID@ in same card
    - If material_card is empty/missing, no material written (user adds manually or via matswap)

(13) COMMON MISTAKES:
    - Forgetting material_card when connection_mode=czm (validation will fail)
    - Using connection_mode=czm with element_type=tshell/shell (not supported)
    - Setting thickness_formula but leaving variables undefined in coord system
    - Not setting shell_thickness for tshell/shell element types
    - Mixing material_card and material_cards[] (use one, not both)
    - Trying to offset shell elements created by prior offset in same operations[] call"

operations.name: wrap
operations.summary: Apply winding tension prestress (hoop + radial stress) for cylindrical parts
operations.description: Apply winding tension prestress to cylindrical parts in cylindrical coordinates. Calculates hoop tension (tangential stress) and radial compression based on layer geometry and wrapping tension. Generates *INITIAL_STRESS_SOLID in separate .dynain file. Used for modeling wire/fiber winding prestress or compression in stacked cylindrical structures.

params.name: config
params.description: 전체 YAML 설정 객체

example.note: Example: wrap_test.yaml in examples/wrap/. Produces cylinder_wrapped.k and cylinder_wrapped.dynain with hoop + radial prestress. Use with 'relax' command for dynamic relaxation before main analysis.

operations.notes:
CRITICAL PARSER QUIRKS:
1. E and nu MUST be specified at YAML top level (not nested under material:). The parser parses material: section separately and does NOT read E/nu from inside material:.
2. target_pid accepts both scalar (target_pid: 1) and bracket list (target_pid: [1,2]) syntax. Parser auto-detects format.
3. center coordinate order: [axis1_coord, axis2_coord] in the plane perpendicular to winding_axis. For axis=z (default), center=[x,y]. For axis=x, center=[y,z]. For axis=y, center=[x,z].
4. tension must be non-zero (validation error if tension == 0.0).
5. targetPids must be non-empty (validation error if empty).
6. Layer ordering (inner→outer by radius) is NOT enforced but a WARNING is emitted if radii are out of order.

PHYSICS MODEL:
- Hoop stress (tangential): σ_θθ = tension / t_elem (uniform within element radial span)
- Radial compression (layer k): σ_rr = -tension / R * (N - k) / N where N = number of layers, R = layer average radius, k = layer index (0=innermost)
- Axial stress: σ_zz = 0 (free)
- Global coordinate transformation: cylindrical (r,θ,z) → Cartesian (x,y,z) via atan2(perpendicular_coords) for θ, then rotate stress tensor

MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE / CONSTRAINTS:
- center (explicit) vs. autoCenter=true (implicit): if center is set in YAML, autoCenter forced to false; if center omitted, autoCenter=true
- axis choice determines which perpendicular axes used for cylindrical coordinates

OUTPUT:
- {output}.k: model with *INITIAL_STRESS_SOLID keyword block (one stress tensor per element)
- {output}.dynain: LS-DYNA dynain file with *INITIAL_STRESS_SOLID card that can be embedded via *INCLUDE or *INITIAL_STRESS_SOLID_ID
- Info message: "[wrap] N layers, tension=X N/mm, axis=Y, center=(A,B), M elements"

ASSEMBLY MODE (operations[].type: wrap):
- Same YAML keys as standalone, parsed in AssemblyConfigReader.cpp lines 1224–1253
- Can mix with other operations (replace, bend, etc.)
- Material E/nu inherited from top-level material: block if not explicitly set per-operation

STANDALONE MODE (KooRemapper wrap config.yaml):
- E/nu parsed at top-level YAML (see AssemblyConfigReader / StandaloneYamlBase)
- Material E/nu required if *INITIAL_STRESS_SOLID includes strain (otherwise stress-only)

RELAX / EQUILIBRATION:
- Output stress is UNbalanced (not in equilibrium). Use 'relax' command (dynamic relaxation) or set dynamicRelaxation: true in assemble config to equilibrate before main FEA
- relax command (standalone): KooRemapper relax config.yaml with level (1–5), mode (explicit/implicit), endtime, drterm parameters

operations.notes:
GOTCHAS & DESIGN NOTES:

1. **Input Requirements**: CNRB file must contain:
   - *CONSTRAINED_NODAL_RIGID_BODY [_TITLE] keyword block
   - NSID pointing to a valid *SET_NODE_LIST with ≥4 nodes
   - At least 2 distinct Z-levels in the hole-node cloud (else skipped with warning)

2. **PNODE (Center Node)**: If PNODE > 0 in the CNRB data line, that node is used as bolt center; otherwise, centroid of NSID nodes is computed. PNODE (if present) is **removed** from the output *NODE section.

3. **Mesh Topology** (O-grid HEX8):
   - **Core**: m × m = (N/4)² square elements (4-sided with inner nodes)
   - **Ring 0**: N elements from core boundary to first outer ring
   - **Additional Rings**: One per distinct R cluster (shaft) or head rings (if head_offset_r > 0)
   - **Total per layer**: m² + N × (number of rings)
   - **Total layers**: (# Z-levels) + (1 if head added, for head top level)

4. **Auto Circumferential Nodes**: If num_circum_nodes = 0:
   - Count max nodes in any Z-level
   - N = max(8, round_to_multiple_of_4(max_nodes_per_level / 4))
   - Ensures N ≥ 8 for acceptable mesh density

5. **Axis Direction Auto-Snap**: PCA detects elongation direction; if abs(axis.x) > 0.9 → snap to (±1, 0, 0), etc. Avoids floating-point tilt artifacts.

6. **Z-Level Grouping**: Nodes are rounded to nearest z_tolerance grid point, then grouped. All rounded Z-values within a level are treated as same cross-section.

7. **Radial Ring Clustering**: Distinct R values (max R per Z-level) are clustered. Running mean used for cluster centers. Each cluster (group of similar R values) becomes one ring. Head rings (if enabled) are additional concentric rings from R_shaft to R_head.

8. **Radius Scale < 1.0**: Ring nodes placed **inside** the hole by factor radius_scale. Critical for Tied Contact to work (maintains gap for contact algorithms). Typical 0.999 → ~0.001 gap at R=3mm.

9. **Head Placement Logic**:
   - If head_position = 'auto' AND rMin_side < rMax_side (comparing R at Z_min vs Z_max), place head at Z_max.
   - If head_position = 'top', always place at Z_max.
   - If head_position = 'bottom', always place at Z_min.
   - If 'none', no head (equivalently, head_offset_r: 0).

10. **Material & Section**: One *MAT_ELASTIC and *SECTION_SOLID per converted CNRB, using fresh secId and matId. Part PID remains same as original CNRB PID.

11. **Tied Contact**: A *SET_NODE_LIST (NSID nodes) and *CONTACT_TIED_SURFACE_TO_SURFACE_OFFSET are generated. Users must ensure conformal or near-conformal mesh between solid bolt surface and surrounding structure.

12. **Multiple CNRBs**: All non-empty CNRBs converted unless targetPids filter is set (not exposed in YAML; C++ API only). Each gets own nodes, elements, part, section, material, contact.

13. **File Modifications**: CNRB blocks removed; PNODE removed from *NODE section; *END marker preserved. All insertion done before *END.

14. **Supported Unit System**: Designed for t/mm/s: E in MPa, RHO in t/mm³, geometry in mm, time in s. Other systems require manual unit conversion on input/output.

15. **Mesh Constraints**: 
    - Inner core cannot exceed first ring radius (forced via inner_radius_ratio)
    - All rings within Z-layer must have distinct, monotonic radii
    - Minimum 4 nodes per CNRB (auto-skipped if fewer)
    - Minimum 2 Z-levels (auto-skipped if 1 level only)

16. **Preset Levels**: No presets or modes; all parameters explicit. No relax/implicit/stabilize modes.

keys.desc: Input K-file containing one or more *CONSTRAINED_NODAL_RIGID_BODY definitions. Each CNRB specifies PID, NSID (node set of hole nodes), PNODE (center point, optional).
Output K-file path. Contains generated HEX8 solid elements, nodes, parts, sections, materials, node sets, and tied contact definitions.
Young's modulus [MPa]. Typical: 200000 (steel 200 GPa). Used to create *MAT_ELASTIC material for each converted CNRB.
Poisson's ratio (0.0–0.5). Typical: 0.3 for steel. Used in *MAT_ELASTIC.
Mass density [t/mm³]. For t/mm/s unit system: 7.85e-9 for steel (= 7850 kg/m³). Used in *MAT_ELASTIC.
Scaling factor for outer ring node radii. Ring radius = detected bolt-hole R × radius_scale. Must be ≤ 1.0 to maintain gap for tied contact (~0.001 gap at 0.999). Typical range: 0.95–0.999.

Number of circumferential nodes per ring (must be multiple of 4). Set to 0 (default) for auto-detection: N = max(8, round_to_4(max_nodes_per_z_level / 4)). Override with explicit value (e.g. 8, 12, 16, 20) to control mesh density.

Core square half-side length divided by first ring radius. Determines central square mesh size relative to bolt hole. Typical: 0.3 (core side ≈ 60% of bolt diameter). Higher ratio → larger core, fewer ring cells; lower → smaller core, more ring cells.
Cylinder axis direction. 'auto' = principal axis detected via PCA of hole-node cloud, then snapped to nearest canonical axis (x, y, or z). Override with 'x', 'y', or 'z' to force a specific axis.
Z-level grouping tolerance [mm]. Nodes within this distance along the cylinder axis are merged into the same cross-section level. Controls layer discretization; smaller = finer Z-discretization.

Radial cluster tolerance [mm]. Groups distinct bolt radii (e.g., stepped bolts with multiple diameters) into clusters. Each cluster → one ring. Nodes within r_tolerance of the previous cluster are merged; clusters farther apart → separate rings. Controls radial ring count.
Bolt head (flange) radius offset [mm]. Head radius = R_shaft + head_offset_r. Set to 0.0 (default) to skip head generation. Typical: 1.0–3.0 for visible head. Must be ≥ 0.
Bolt head axial (Z-direction) thickness [mm]. Only used if head_offset_r > 0. Extra Z-level added at shaft extremity ± head_thickness. Typical: 1.0–3.0. Must be > 0.
'auto' = place head at Z_max (or at end with larger radius if auto-selected). 'top' = force Z_max side. 'bottom' = force Z_min side. 'none' = disable head (same as head_offset_r: 0).

operations.name: elform
operations.summary: Change element formulation (ELFORM) in LS-DYNA *SECTION_* cards
operations.description: Modifies ELFORM (element formulation) parameters in *SECTION_SOLID or *SECTION_SHELL keyword cards. Supports linear-to-linear (ELFORM change only), linear-to-quadratic (element conversion), and quadratic-to-linear (element downgrade) transitions. Target parts can be specified individually or as ranges (e.g., target_pid: 1-5). When target_pid or target_pids is omitted, applies to all parts.

params.name: config
params.description: YAML configuration object containing base_model, output, and operations array with elform operations

example.note: Changes all elements to ELFORM 2 (full integration). Run in examples/elform/ directory.

operations.notes:
**Key points:**

- **target_elform is required** and can be a numeric string or case-sensitive alias. Aliases (e.g., 'tet10', 'fully_integrated', 'quad8') map to specific numeric ELFORM codes defined in the source.

- **target_pid defaults to 0 (all parts)**. Use target_pid or target_pids to restrict to specific parts. Both cannot be specified simultaneously in typical usage.

- **Numeric ELFORM 23 is ambiguous** (maps to both HEX20 for solids and QUAD8 for shells). Auto-detection examines the target part's element types (QUAD4 = shell, HEX8/TET4 = solid) to disambiguate.

- **Three operation modes exist:**
  1. **SAME_ORDER** (default): Both source and target are linear, or both quadratic. Only the *SECTION card's ELFORM field is modified; no mesh connectivity change.
  2. **UPGRADE**: Target is quadratic (ELFORM 16/17/23/24) and source is linear. Triggers full element conversion (adds mid-order nodes via Tet10Convert mechanism).
  3. **DOWNGRADE**: Source has quadratic elements and target is linear. Mid-order nodes are removed from the mesh; element connectivity is simplified.

- **Alias case sensitivity**: Alias strings are case-sensitive. 'tet10' works; 'Tet10' or 'TET10' will fail with "Unknown ELFORM alias" error.

- **target_pids list syntax**: Supports comma-separated list, space-separated list, or range notation (e.g., '1-5' expands to [1,2,3,4,5]). YAML list format (- 1 \\n - 2) also accepted.

- **Element type detection**: The operation auto-determines if a numeric ELFORM is for solids or shells by checking if the target parts contain QUAD4 (shell) vs HEX8/TET4 (solid) elements. If ambiguous or no elements exist, it defaults to solid."

keys.desc: Operation type; must be 'elform'
Single part ID to modify (0 or omit = all parts; -1 means use target_pids list)
List of part IDs to modify (alternative to target_pid for multiple parts). Expands ranges like '1-5' to [1,2,3,4,5]

Target ELFORM value: either numeric (1,2,3,...,17,23,24) or alias string (constant_stress, fully_integrated, tet4, tet10, hex20, belytschko_tsay, fully_integrated_shell, hughes_liu, quad8, tria6). Alias format is case-sensitive. For numeric forms, the type (solid vs shell) is auto-detected from target part elements.

presets.name: Shell Formulations

presets.name: Linear-only ELFORM change

presets.name: Linear-to-Quadratic upgrade

operations.name: disconnect
operations.summary: Decohere conformal mesh interface for fracture modeling by splitting shared nodes at part boundaries.
operations.description: Duplicates shared nodes at part boundaries to create discontinuous interfaces for fracture and cohesive zone modeling. Three modes: full (peridynamics), czm (cohesive zone elements), mefem (mesh-free enrichment). Primarily used with LS-DYNA fracture analysis.

params.name: config
params.description: Complete YAML configuration object with base_model, output, and operations array

example.note: Example uses two_hex_2part.k from examples/disconnect. Mode 'czm' requires cohesive_part_id and optionally failure_strain. Mode 'full' splits all nodes without cohesive elements. Mode 'mefem' adds peridynamic elements and supports failure_strain.

operations.notes: MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE: mode=full vs czm/mefem. Full mode ignores cohesive_part_id and failure_strain. CZM mode requires inter-part faces (different PIDs sharing mesh faces); fails if no boundaries found. MEFEM mode currently inserts *ELEMENT_CONSTRAINT_DISTRIBUTED_COUPLE (not shown in example yet). IMPORTANT: disconnect is EMBEDDED in operations[] array within assemble command; it is not a standalone CLI command. target_pid=0 means all PIDs participate in active element detection, but only inter-part boundaries trigger node duplication in czm/mefem. Full mode creates new nodes for ALL elements in target_pid, regardless of boundaries. Both solid (HEX8/TET4/PENTA6) and shell (QUAD4) elements supported. Duplicate nodes are collocated (same XYZ) at original position — separation is by part connectivity only, not physical offset.

operations.notes:
**타겟 선택 규칙:**
- target_pid 또는 target_name 중 최소 하나 필수 (둘 다 0/공백이면 오류).
- target_pids 사용시 각 ID마다 개별 target으로 자동 확장.
- target_name은 와일드카드(*) 지원; exclude_name과 조합 가능 (매칭된 항목 중 제외).

**바운딩박스 확장 우선순위 (높→낮):**
1. bbox_scale_r/s/t (축별 배율, 0이면 다음 단계)
2. bbox_scale (균일 배율, 0이면 다음)
3. offset >= 0 (고정값)
4. 기본값: element_size (각 축별)

**제약사항:**
- element_size > 0 필수 (0 이하 오류).
- targets[] 비어있으면 오류.
- pr, ps, pt >= 1 (NURBS 차수).
- nisr, niss, nist >= 1 (적분점).
- ir: 0 또는 1만 유효.
- IGA와 FE 파트는 반드시 다른 MID(재료ID) 사용 (LS-DYNA 요구사항).

**MID 격리:**
IGA 파트와 기존 FE 파트가 같은 MID를 사용하면 해석 오류 발생. 출력된 _iga_p{pid}.k 파일의 MID는 자동 조정되거나 별도로 지정 필요.

**멀티 PID 확장:**
target_pids: [1, 2, 3]으로 지정하면 내부에서 target_pid: 1, target_pid: 2, target_pid: 3으로 자동 확장.

**복셀 크기 해석:**
element_size = 4.0 → r/s/t 방향 각각 4.0 단위 크기 복셀 생성. 작을수록 정밀하나 계산량 증가.

**출력 구조:**
- <output>.k: 원본 FE 유지 + *INCLUDE로 IGA 파일 참조.
- <output>_iga_p{pid}.k: 각 파트별 IGA NURBS 박스 (*IGA_DEV_VOLUME_XYZ 포함).

operations.name: tetremesh
operations.summary: TET4 local remesh: improve quality via Laplacian smoothing/swap (localimprove) or constrained Delaunay (tetgen)
operations.description: TET4 local remesh: improves tetrahedral mesh quality via Laplacian smoothing/face-edge swap (localimprove backend) or constrained Delaunay tetrahedralization (tetgen backend). Identifies poorly-shaped elements (min Jacobian, aspect ratio) or explicitly selected elements, extracts local patches, and improves them while preserving multi-material boundaries. Supports report-only mode and iterative remeshing until target quality is reached.

params.name: config
params.description: 전체 YAML 설정 객체 (config.yaml 로 기록되어 실행됨)

example.note: Two TET4 elements from examples/tet10/. Uses localimprove backend to improve Jacobian. Set backend:tetgen to use TetGen (requires KOOREMAPPER_BUILD_TETGEN). Set report_only:true to scan quality without changes. selection.mode can be 'bad_quality' (auto-detect poor elements) or 'explicit_ids' (user element_ids list). iterate section enables iterative remesh until quality_target met.

operations.notes: CRITICAL GOTCHAS: (1) **Scaled Jacobian interpretation**: 1.0=perfect regular tet, 0.0=degenerate, <0=inverted. Threshold 0.2 is *minimum acceptable*, not aspirational. (2) **Iterative mode** keeps BEST mesh state (if keep_best=true), not the final state—check best_iteration in output. (3) **fallback backend** only retries failed patches; primary backend success is still used if it works. (4) **Multi-material boundaries**: preserve_multi_material=true blocks remeshing across PID edges—this can constrain local patches and reduce quality gains if material boundaries cut through bad elements. (5) **Element expansion**: ring_mode='node' extracts larger neighborhoods than 'face'; choose based on patch size needs. (6) **Selection mode default** is bad_quality—explicit_ids requires non-empty element_ids list; empty element_ids with explicit_ids mode logs warning but continues (no-op). (7) **surface_move_tolerance=0.0 (default)** allows full boundary movement; positive values lock boundary nodes closer to original position, which may prevent quality improvements. (8) **TetGen AGPL license**: requires explicit compile flag KOOREMAPPER_BUILD_TETGEN; some deployments may not include it. Check backend availability in logs. (9) **Report-only mode** (report_only=true) skips output file write—useful for quality audits without mesh changes. (10) **Ring_expand=0 is invalid**; minimum is 1."

keys.desc: Input K file path; TET4/HEX8/mixed elements loaded for mesh quality analysis
Output K file path; remeshed mesh written here (only if report_only=false)
Primary remeshing backend. localimprove: Laplacian smoothing + face/edge flips, no dependencies. tetgen: constrained Delaunay (AGPL, requires compile flag ON). Default localimprove (always available)
Secondary backend if primary fails on a patch. Empty string (default) disables fallback. When set, if backend fails on a patch, attempt retry with fallback backend
If true: scan mesh quality and report statistics without modifying or writing output. Useful for quality audits
Part IDs to remesh; empty array (default) processes all parts. Restrict remeshing to specific material parts via integer list [1, 2, 3]
Element selection strategy. bad_quality: auto-detect poorly-shaped elements. explicit_ids: use element_ids array as seed set. Note: 'explicit' is an alias for 'explicit_ids'
Explicit element IDs to include in remesh patches (used only if selection_mode=explicit_ids). Specify as integer list [10, 20, 30]
Neighborhood extraction mode. node: extract elements via node adjacency (larger patches). face: extract via face adjacency (smaller patches, tighter boundaries)
Scaled Jacobian quality threshold (0.0=degenerate, 1.0=perfect tet). Elements below this marked as bad_quality. Typical thresholds: <0.1 very poor, 0.2-0.5 acceptable, >0.7 excellent
Maximum aspect ratio threshold (longest edge / shortest edge). Elements exceeding this ratio flagged for remesh when using bad_quality mode. Higher = more lenient (e.g., 10.0)
Neighborhood expansion rings around selected elements. Higher = larger patches, longer processing. Typical range 1-3. Applies to both bad_quality and explicit_ids modes
Surface flatness tolerance in degrees for boundary preservation. Controls how much patch surface can deviate from original. Lower = stricter boundary fidelity
Maximum boundary node displacement tolerance (model units). Zero (default) allows surface nodes to move freely within flatness_deg constraint. Positive values restrict node movement
If true: prevent remeshing across material boundaries (preserve interface edges between different PIDs). If false: allow mixing of different materials in patch
Laplacian smoothing iteration count (localimprove only). Higher = more smoothing, slower. Typical range 1-10. Improves element shape after flips
Maximum outer improvement loop iterations (localimprove only). Repeat flip+smooth cycles up to this count until convergence. Typical 2-5
If true: allow element subdivision during improvement (localimprove may split elements). If false: improvement via flips and smoothing only
TetGen quality ratio parameter (q flag). Controls minimum dihedral angle enforcement. Typical 1.0-2.0. Higher = stricter quality, longer runtime
TetGen minimum dihedral angle (degrees). Enforces all dihedral angles >= this value. Typical 5.0-20.0. Higher = better quality but may fail on constrained patches

Enable iterative remesh mode as simple boolean flag. Set to true for default iterative behavior with max_iterations=10, quality_target=0.3, convergence_tol=0.01, keep_best=true. To customize iteration parameters, use the iterate section instead

Maximum iterations for iterative remesh mode (nested under iterate section). Loop until quality_target reached or this limit exhausted. Typical 5-20. Any sub-key under iterate section enables iteration
Target minimum Jacobian in iterative mode (nested under iterate section). Iteration stops when all elements >= this value or max_iterations exhausted. Typical 0.2-0.5
Convergence tolerance for early stopping in iterative mode (nested under iterate section). If improvement between iterations < this, stop early. Typical 0.005-0.05
If true in iterative mode (nested under iterate section): keep best mesh state across all iterations. If false: keep final state only
Element selection strategy within selection section. Equivalent to top-level selection_mode key
Explicit element IDs within selection section. Equivalent to top-level element_ids key
Neighborhood expansion rings within selection section. Equivalent to patch.ring_expand key. Can be specified in either location
Neighborhood extraction mode within selection section. Equivalent to top-level ring_mode key

operations.summary: TET4 Gmsh-based adaptive remesh with quality control
operations.description: TET4 Gmsh-based adaptive remesh with quality control. Gmsh-driven adaptive TET4 remesh with element quality improvement via scaled-Jacobian checking and optional patch polishing. Extracts boundary STL, runs Gmsh with configurable 3D algorithms, and splices remeshed elements back into the model. Supports thin-solid detection, distance-field size adaptation, and boundary node handling strategies.

example.note: 실행 검증된 예제 (입력: tetramesh.k)

operations.notes:
CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:
- Gmsh executable must be placed at dist/gmsh/gmsh.exe or dist/gmsh-<ver>/gmsh.exe relative to KooRemapper executable. Without it, operation fails immediately.
- Input must be TET4 elements or degenerate HEX8 (nodes[3..7] all equal node[3]).

SECTION HEADERS (optional YAML organization):
All top-level keys can also be nested under optional section headers for readability: [material], [adaptive], [gmsh], [boundary], [quality]. Keys under sections use slightly different names:
- Under [boundary]: use 'nodes' instead of 'boundary_nodes'
- Other section keys match top-level names (e.g., 'min_dt', 'E', 'nu' under [material]).

AUTO-DETECTION & GEOMETRY:
- lc_min auto-calc: If lc_min < 0 AND all of (min_dt, density, E, nu) > 0, computed from wave speed. Otherwise: lc_min = min(edge_min*0.8, lc_target*0.2).
- THIN SOLID DETECTION: If min_bbox_dimension < avg_bbox_dimension * 0.3, geomThin=true → Mesh 2 skipped, 4-corner in-plane field used, Netgen passes skipped, autoRefineSurface=1 if needed.
- AUTO refine_surface: Only applies when refine_surface=-1. Disabled for normal geometry (Mesh 2 handles it); applies 1 level for thin geometry if edge_avg > lc_target*1.5.

DISTANCE FIELD SCALING (when adaptive=true):
- Normal geometry: 8-corner field. DistMin = lcMinField*2, DistMax = lcMinField * decay_factor.
- Thin geometry (thin axis detected): 4-corner in-plane field. DistMin = lcMinField*2, DistMax = lcMinField*4 (smaller decay to avoid flooding thin dim).

POLISH MODE (experimental):
- Requires polish=true.
- Identifies connected components of bad elements (Jac < polish_jac).
- Each component expanded 2 rings, then patch re-meshed independently.
- DUAL QUALITY GATES (both must pass to accept):
  1. Min Jacobian retention: new_min_jac >= orig_min_jac * 0.95
  2. Bad-element reduction: new_bad_count < orig_bad_count
- If either gate fails, patch is discarded and original elements kept.
- Mesh 2 skipped for patches; uses serial Delaunay (safer for small patches).

BOUNDARY NODES:
- free: all Gmsh nodes receive new sequential IDs (maxNodeId+1, maxNodeId+2, ...). Useful for independent part re-meshes.
- fixed: Gmsh surface nodes matched to original model boundary nodes by coordinate (within snap_tolerance). Interior nodes get new IDs. Preserves node IDs at the interface for contact definitions.
- snap: All Gmsh nodes get new IDs, but boundary nodes near adjacent parts are snapped to those part's nodes (within snap_tolerance). Allows loose coupling without strict coordinate matching.

GOTCHAS & MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE:
- lc_min AND (min_dt, density, E, nu): if lc_min >= 0, dt-based calculation is skipped (explicit value takes priority).
- optimize_netgen & optimize_passes: both skipped automatically for thin geometry regardless of setting.
- refine_surface=-1 AND geomThin: auto refinement only applies to thin geometry. Normal geometry uses Mesh 2 instead.
- polish=true AND 90° corners: if geometry has unrounded 90° corners, polish often cannot reduce bad elements (theoretical min ~0.03), so patches will be rejected.

GMSH TIMEOUT & FAILURES:
- No explicit timeout; Gmsh may hang on malformed STL or recursive ClassifySurfaces. If hung, Ctrl+C and check STL for open edges / non-manifold geometry.
- Exit code 1 from Gmsh is often OK (warnings like ClassifySurfaces recursion). Check if .msh file was written before failing.

PERFORMANCE HINTS:
- Large meshes (100k+ TET4) take minutes. Use lc_target wisely to control output size.
- Thin geometry disables Mesh 2 and Netgen, speeding up processing significantly.
- Polish mode adds significant time; use sparingly on already-good meshes.

keys.desc: Input LS-DYNA .k file containing the TET4 part to remesh
Output LS-DYNA .k file with remeshed part (other parts preserved)
Part ID of the TET4 element part to remesh
Target average element size for remesh (model units). Sets the background field size for the interior mesh.
Minimum element size; -1 = auto from edge_min*0.8 or dt-based calculation. Controls the finest elements near 90° corners via the distance field.
Maximum element size; -1 = lc_target * 2. Hard ceiling on all elements (CharacteristicLengthMax).
LS-DYNA explicit time step lower bound (seconds). Used with density, E, nu to compute lc_min via wave speed: lc = dt * sqrt(E*(1-nu) / (rho*(1+nu)*(1-2*nu)))
Material density (t/mm³). Required when min_dt is set for dt-based lc_min calculation.
Young's modulus (MPa). Required when min_dt is set for dt-based lc_min calculation.
Poisson's ratio (dimensionless). Required when min_dt is set for dt-based lc_min calculation.
Minimum element layers through the thin dimension for thin-solid handling. When thin geometry is detected (min_bbox < avg_bbox*0.3), this controls the lcMinField = thin_dimension / min_layers_thin.
Enable MathEval distance-field size adaptation around bounding-box corners. When true, emits a distance formula to refine elements near 90° corners.
Corner refinement decay distance = lc_min * decay_factor. Controls the Threshold field DistMax; larger values spread the fine zone further from corners.

Boundary node handling strategy: 'free' assigns new IDs to all Gmsh nodes; 'fixed' matches Gmsh boundary nodes to original model nodes by coordinate (within snap_tolerance); 'snap' snaps new boundary nodes to adjacent part nodes within snap_tolerance.
Search radius (model units) for snap mode boundary node merging and fixed-mode coordinate matching tolerance.
Gmsh 3D mesh algorithm: 'hxt' = parallel hybrid (fast, default), 'frontal3d' = advancing front, 'del3d' = Delaunay (serial). Stored as Mesh.Algorithm3D {10, 4, 1} in the .geo script.
Enable Gmsh built-in Netgen optimization after Mesh 3 (sets Mesh.OptimizeNetgen). Skipped automatically for thin geometry.
Number of additional OptimizeMesh 'Netgen' passes after Mesh 3. Skipped for thin geometry (geomThin=true).
Report scaled-Jacobian quality statistics after remesh (min, avg, max Jacobian and count of elements below warn_min_jac).
Warn if elements have scaled Jacobian below this threshold. Also used in polish mode to identify 'bad' elements for re-meshing.

STL surface refinement levels: -1 = auto-detect (1 level for thin geom if edge_avg > lc_target*1.5, 0 for normal geom), 0 = off, 1-3 = conforming feature-edge bisection (subdivides only dihedral > 40° edges).
Laplacian smoothing steps on STL feature-edge vertices (dihedral > 40°); 0 = off. Rounds 90° corners slightly to raise minimum Jacobian.
Enable local bad-element patch re-meshing (experimental). When true, identifies connected clusters of elements with Jacobian < polish_jac and re-meshes them locally if quality gates pass.
Polish target: identifies elements with scaled Jacobian below this threshold as candidates for patch re-meshing.
Maximum iterations of patch polishing. Each iteration finds new bad clusters and attempts re-mesh if no improvements remain, loop exits.

operations.name: matswap
operations.summary: Replace material bundle (MAT/HOURGLASS/DEFINE_CURVE/SECTION) for one or more parts
operations.description: Replace material bundle (MAT/HOURGLASS/DEFINE_CURVE/SECTION) for one or more parts. Swaps a complete material bundle from a bundle file to target parts by PID or by MID (material ID). Automatically handles ID collision avoidance, orphaned card removal, and parameter resolution via *PARAMETER block. Supports single operation or integration into assemble workflow. Optional post-optimization for rubber properties (tssfac control).

params.name: config
params.description: Complete YAML configuration object with model, output, and swaps array

example.note: Invoked as: KooRemapper matswap config.yaml where config.yaml contains the YAML structure above

operations.notes: **Bundle File Format Requirement:** Bundle must contain a *PARAMETER block with parameter names prefixed by ID type:  HGID*, LCID*, SECID*, MID*, PID*. The parser detects the type by prefix (case-insensitive) and allocates new IDs accordingly (HGID/LCID/SECID always auto-increment; MID reuses orphan IDs when safe).  **ID Allocation Logic:** (1) HGID/LCID/SECID: always allocate new IDs (model max + 1). (2) MID: if old MID is shared (used by other parts), allocate new; if orphan (used only by target), reuse old ID. (3) PID parameters in bundle are ignored. **Orphan Removal:** Old *MAT_, *SECTION, *HOURGLASS cards are automatically removed ONLY if they are not shared with non-target parts. (4) **Parameter Resolution:** All parameter references (&PARAM_NAME) in bundle cards are resolved to new IDs before insertion. (5) **Output:** Resolved cards inserted just before *END. Output file has no *PARAMETER block. **PID vs MID Targeting:** pid/pids swaps full material+section+hourglass bundle; mid/mids swaps only material+hourglass+curves (no section). **Mutually Exclusive Options:** Only ONE of pid/pids/mid/mids/swap_all per swap operation. **optimize=rubber:** Modifies CONTACT friction, CONTROL_HOURGLASS IHQ, and CONTROL_TIMESTEP TSSFAC for rubber parts. **Legacy Positional Interface:** Still supported: KooRemapper matswap model.k bundle.k pid output.k (4 args). **Integration:** matswap can be used as operation type in assemble workflow (see examples/matswap/04_assemble_integration.yaml)."

Single MID to target. Mutually exclusive with pid, pids, mids, swap_all. Swaps MAT+HOURGLASS+DEFINE_CURVE ONLY (no SECTION). Used to update only material properties, keeping section unchanged.

THERMAL EXPANSION: thermal: true inserts *MAT_THERMAL_ISOTROPIC and *MAT_ADD_THERMAL_EXPANSION pairs with auto-linked TMID.
